toolsPanel_restrictedDescription: Chrome blocks content scripts on chrome:// pages, other extensions' pages, the Chrome Web Store, and its built-in PDF viewer — there is no way for this or any extension to reach in, so this tab will never have page tools, no matter what the page itself supports. Chat and MCP server tools still work here.
toolsPanel_webmcpOffTitle: WebMCP is off in this browser
toolsPanel_webmcpOffDescription: document.modelContext doesn't exist here — WebMCP is off by default in Chrome and needs --enable-features=WebMCP, the chrome://flags/#enable-webmcp-testing toggle, or a per-origin origin-trial token before a page can use it at all. This is different from a page simply not registering any tools — there was nothing here to even ask.
toolsPanel_noPageToolsDescription1: This is expected — most sites don't speak WebMCP yet. It's a proposed web standard that lets a page expose specific actions and page-state readers — "add a note", "read the cart total" — on document.modelContext, so an AI agent can call them directly instead of a human clicking through the UI. It's the same idea as MCP, but for what a website itself chooses to offer, rather than a separate server.
toolsPanel_noPageToolsDescription2: A site opts in by calling registerTool() in its own page script. If this page did, its tools would show up here the moment it registers them — nothing to refresh or configure on your end.
toolsPanel_noServerToolsDescription: Add and enable a server from the options page's MCP Servers section — a slow, unreachable, or not-yet-permitted server simply contributes no tools here rather than blocking anything.

mcpServersSection_description: An MCP server exposes tools the model can call that have nothing to do with the current page — a ticket tracker, a search index, an internal service. Its tools are merged into the same list the page's own tools appear in, namespaced by server so nothing collides — but a server tool call is judged by its own, separate, stricter approval policy, not the page's (decisions/20-approval-policy-is-per-tool-source.md). See "MCP server tool approval" above.

mcpServersSection_emptyDescription: Only remote HTTP/SSE MCP servers are supported here — this extension can't spawn or speak to a local stdio process the way a desktop MCP client can. To reach a stdio-only server, put an off-the-shelf stdio-to-HTTP proxy in front of it and add the proxy's URL below instead.

settingsSection_approvalDescription: Controls when a tool call from the page's own WebMCP tools runs immediately versus waiting for you to approve it first (decisions/05-tool-approval-policy.md).
settingsSection_defaultPolicyDescription: Tools the page marks readOnlyHint: true run automatically, shown as a collapsed card in the chat. Every other tool call — including ones with no annotation at all — waits for you to approve it before it runs.
settingsSection_alwaysConfirmPolicyDescr: Every tool call waits for your approval, even ones the page marks read-only. Slower, but nothing runs without you seeing it first.
settingsSection_autoRunAllPolicyDescript: Every tool call runs immediately, with no approval step at all — including calls that submit forms, delete data, send messages, or otherwise change a live, logged-in site. The model can act on your behalf and you get no chance to review a call before it happens. Only choose this if you fully trust both the model you're chatting with and every site you open the side panel on.
settingsSection_safetyAnnotationsNotice: Tool safety annotations like readOnlyHint are supplied by the page itself, not verified by the extension — a hostile page can label a genuinely destructive tool "read-only" to slip it past this policy. This setting is UX guidance for the common case, not a security boundary; the actual boundary is which sites you've chosen to open the side panel on and grant this extension permission to reach. Every call, auto-run or approved, is still recorded in the tool-call log so nothing happens invisibly.
settingsSection_mcpApprovalDescription: A SEPARATE setting from "Tool approval" above (decisions/20-approval-policy-is-per-tool-source.md) — controls when a call to one of your configured MCP servers' tools runs immediately versus waiting for your approval. Changing the page policy above never affects this one, or the other way around.
settingsSection_mcpAlwaysConfirmDescript: Every MCP server tool call waits for your approval, regardless of what the server itself claims about being read-only. A remote service's self-report isn't something you can see the effect of the way you can a page, so this is the strictest of the three options here — deliberately stricter than the page policy's default above.
settingsSection_mcpSafetyNotice: A remote server is not something you're looking at the way you are the current page — you have no ambient evidence a call actually was read-only, and its blast radius can be an account, a repo, or a ticket queue rather than one tab. That is why this policy defaults to "Always confirm" rather than mirroring the page policy's default, and why the two settings are kept fully independent. Manage which servers are configured from the MCP Servers section below.
settingsSection_mcpTrustReadOnlyDescript: Tools an MCP server marks readOnlyHint: true run automatically, shown as a collapsed card in the chat, same as the page policy's default. Only choose this for servers you trust to report that hint honestly — it's a claim the server makes about itself, not something this extension verifies.
settingsSection_mcpAutoRunAllDescription: Every MCP server tool call runs immediately, no approval step at all — including calls that modify or delete data on a service authenticated as you, invisibly to whatever you're currently looking at. Only choose this if you fully trust every server you've added below.
